title: Amoxicillin 250mg Capsules (PIL)
paraphrase_text: I think I'm meant to take the capsules exactly as the doctor or pharmacist told me, swallowing them whole with water and spacing the doses about 4 hours apart. If I miss a dose, I should take it when I remember, but not take a double dose to catch up. I need to finish the whole course even if I feel better, and I shouldn't share the medicine with anyone else. If I get a bad rash, swelling of my face or throat, trouble breathing, or severe diarrhoea, I should stop taking it and see a doctor straight away.

title: NHS Antibiotics condition page
paraphrase_text: I think I'm meant to take my antibiotics exactly as the packet or my doctor or pharmacist says, and not skip them just because I feel better. If I miss a dose, I should take it when I remember, unless the next one is nearly due, in which case I skip it. I must never take two doses to catch up. I shouldn't use antibiotics for colds, flu, or coughs, and I should never take someone else's pills. If I get a rash, start wheezing, have trouble breathing, or my face or throat swells, I need to call 999 straight away.

title: NHS Paracetamol for adults dosing page
paraphrase_text: What I understood is that I can take paracetamol for pain or a high temperature, but I shouldn't keep taking it for more than 3 days unless a doctor tells me to. I need to check the packet for how much to take, and I shouldn't take it with other medicines that have paracetamol in them, like cold and flu tablets, because that could be too much. If I take too much, I should call 111 and not drive myself to A&E, and I should bring the packet with me. If I notice a swollen throat, a itchy rash, yellow skin or eyes, or bruising and nosebleeds, I should call 111.

title: NHS Ibuprofen for adults dosing page
paraphrase_text: I think I'm supposed to use ibuprofen for pain or swelling, but only the smallest amount I need for the shortest time. If it's tablets or capsules, I shouldn't keep taking them for more than 10 days unless a doctor tells me to. I shouldn't take aspirin or naproxen with it, and I should try paracetamol first if I can. If I take too much, or I get tummy pain, black sticky poo, or swelling in my face or throat, I should call 111 straight away.

title: Paracetamol duration (SYNTHETIC - reversed min/max)
paraphrase_text: I think I'm supposed to keep taking the paracetamol for at least 3 days and not stop before then, unless my doctor tells me something different. I shouldn't take it along with other medicines that already have paracetamol in them, like cold and flu tablets, because I could end up taking too much. If I think I've taken too much, I should call NHS 111 and take the packet with me.
method_source_phrase: Paracetamol shouldn't be stopped before 3 days are up, unless your doctor hasn't said otherwise.
method_explanation: The reader concluded they must keep taking paracetamol for at least 3 days, which is the opposite of the real guidance (a 3-day maximum without doctor advice). Acting on this could lead to prolonged use and a risk of liver damage.

title: Ibuprofen duration (SYNTHETIC - reversed min/max)
paraphrase_text: I think I'm supposed to keep taking the ibuprofen tablets or capsules for at least 10 days and not stop before then, unless my doctor has said not to. I also read that I should use the smallest dose for the shortest time I need it, so I'd probably take the lowest amount that helps. If my pain gets worse or doesn't go away, I should see my GP. I'd also watch for stomach pain, black sticky poo, or swelling in my ankles.
method_source_phrase: ibuprofen tablets and capsules are not to be discontinued ahead of the 10-day mark
method_explanation: The reader interpreted the double-negative sentence as a minimum 10-day course ('keep taking for at least 10 days'). The real intent is a 10-day maximum unless a doctor advises otherwise, so the reader may take ibuprofen for too long. That raises the risk of stomach ulcers, bleeding and kidney harm.

title: Amoxicillin missed dose (SYNTHETIC - double negative)
paraphrase_text: If I forget a dose, I should take it as soon as I remember. After that, I should wait at least half the usual gap before my next dose. If I've missed more than one dose in a row, I should take a double dose to catch up. I'd keep taking it for as long as the doctor said, even if I feel better.
method_source_phrase: never skip doubling up if you've missed more than one in a row
method_explanation: The reader concluded they should take a double dose after multiple missed doses, which is the opposite of the standard 'do not take a double dose' guidance, and doubling up risks overdose side effects. The reader also resolved 'half the normal interval' as a safe minimum wait, though the leaflet requires doses at least 4 hours apart.

title: Antibiotics missed dose (SYNTHETIC - double negative)
paraphrase_text: If I miss a dose, I think the leaflet is saying I can take two next time if my next dose is nearly due anyway. I'd just make sure I don't leave more than one missed dose uncorrected. I'd take my antibiotics as the packet says, and if I took an extra dose by accident I'd call my GP or NHS 111 if I was worried.
method_source_phrase: Missing a dose isn't a reason not to take two next time
method_explanation: The reader resolved the double negative as permission to take a double dose after a missed one, planning to take two doses next time when the next dose is nearly due. This is the opposite of safe guidance, which is to skip the missed dose and never double up, and it raises the risk of side effects from doses taken too close together.
